title: Duluth Heat Pump Rebates 2026: Minnesota Power $1,000 Cold-Climate Rebate
desc: Duluth heat pump rebates for 2026 from Minnesota Power: $1,000 for cold-climate ducted and ductless systems, $400 for standard ones, ground source up to $1,000 per ton.
lead: A Duluth winter is a hard test for a heat pump. Minnesota Power pays $1,000 for a cold-climate system, which is more than double what it pays for a standard one. We read its heat pump pages on October 6, 2026. The rules are short, and a participating contractor does the paperwork.
cards_heading: What heat pump rebates pay in Duluth
cards_intro: These amounts are for 2026 purchases. Minnesota Power says the rebate cannot be more than 75 percent of the cost of product and labor, and the offer can be withdrawn without notice.

cards.title: Cold-climate heat pump, ducted or ductless
cards.note: The system must stay efficient down to at least 5 degrees Fahrenheit. Reconditioned or resale equipment does not qualify.

cards.title: Standard heat pump, ducted or ductless
cards.note: Same rules, for a unit that is not cold-climate rated.

cards.title: Heat pump tune-up
cards.note: For servicing an existing heat pump.

cards.title: Ground source heat pump
cards.amount: $800 per ton ($1,000 with a Master Installer)
cards.note: Open or closed loop. Hookups to an existing non-electric heating system qualify from April 1, 2026.

cards.title: Dual Fuel electric rate
cards.note: For electric heat with a backup. Standard and Plus versions.

cards.title: State heat pump rebate
cards.note: The state lists a program, but its page was behind a bot check.

after_cards:
Working it out

A $14,000 cold-climate system earns $1,000, because 75 percent of the cost is $10,500, which is far higher than the rebate. A ground source system of 4 tons earns 4 x $800 = $3,200, or 4 x $1,000 = $4,000 with a Master Installer.
sections: The Census Bureau's American Community Survey for 2020 to 2024 counts 39,978 homes in Duluth. About 72% heat with natural gas from a utility line, 19% with electricity, 4% with fuel oil and 3% with bottled gas. About 78% were built before 1980 and 43% before 1940. Fuel oil and bottled gas are about 7% of homes together, and these are the homes most likely to see a big drop in their heating bill from a heat pump. The census table does not give prices, so we cannot say how much any home would save.

Minnesota Power explains that a cold-climate heat pump is a newer kind that gives heat at high efficiency in subzero temperatures. Its rebate rule is simple: the system must keep working efficiently down to at least 5 degrees Fahrenheit. The company says to ask a participating contractor which models qualify. You can still choose a standard unit and take $400, but it may not carry you through a deep cold snap.

Whatever you choose, ask the contractor to show the unit's heating output at the coldest temperatures where you live, and to size the system to the heat your house loses, not to the size of the old furnace.

Keep a backup for the coldest days unless the contractor shows in writing that the heat pump alone can do it. Many homes keep the furnace or boiler. The Dual Fuel rate pairs well with that. You get a lower electric price and accept brief interruptions when electricity is scarce and expensive. The page says you must be ready to heat with a non-electric backup, or have enough stored heat, during interruptions.

Purchases must be made and installed by December 31, 2026. The contractor must be a participating contractor, and the company lists them on its site. Allow eight to ten weeks for the check. If you give a valid email address on the application, extra payment choices such as a prepaid card may appear. For help with the status of a rebate, the company gives a toll-free phone line on its page.
claim_heading: How to claim a Duluth heat pump rebate
claim_steps: Confirm Minnesota Power or a participating utility sends your electric bill.
Get quotes from participating contractors for a cold-climate system.
Ask each contractor to show the cold-weather rating and to size the unit to your home.
Have the system installed by December 31, 2026.
Let the contractor file the rebate for you, and wait eight to ten weeks.
faq: How much does Minnesota Power pay for a heat pump in Duluth?
$1,000 for a cold-climate model, ducted or ductless, and $400 for a standard model.
Yes. Minnesota Power says the rebate cannot be more than 75 percent of project cost including product and labor.
Can I use the rebate with a gas furnace?
The page does not exclude it. A heat pump with a furnace backup is common. Ground source systems tied to an existing non-electric system qualify from April 1, 2026.
We could not confirm it, and the state's federal rebates say they have not launched.
